customer_question: Why are there 16 Inter-Layer Dependency (IDL) errors when running the SIG Consistency Check on our new design that uses A&W Bluetooth Stack 5.4 Host QDID with an existing v5.2 Controller QDID?
question_variants: The Consistency Check shows 16 IDLs — what caused them?
We combined A&W 5.4 Host with a v5.2 Controller QDID and got IDL errors
How do we resolve version mismatch IDLs between Host Stack and Controller?
actual_issue: A&W Bluetooth Stack QDID version 5.4 was paired with a Controller QDID that covers Bluetooth v5.2. The SIG Consistency Check detects that the Host Stack's GAP ICS asserts support for features introduced in v5.3 and v5.4 (e.g., extended advertising enhancements, isochronous channels) that are not reflected in the v5.2 Controller LL ICS. This version mismatch generates 16 IDL (Inter-Layer Dependency) violations.
plain_english_explanation: The Host Stack QDID and Controller QDID must cover the same Bluetooth specification version. When the Host Stack is a newer version than the Controller, the Host's ICS claims features the Controller does not support, and the SIG Consistency Check flags every such conflict as an IDL. Using a v5.4 Host Stack with a v5.2 Controller QDID produces 16 such conflicts.
consultant_answer: Use the A&W Bluetooth Stack v5.2 QDID instead of v5.4. The v5.2 QDID's ICS aligns with the v5.2 Controller QDID and eliminates the version mismatch IDLs. Alternatively, upgrade the Controller to a v5.4-equivalent QDID.
decision_logic: IDLs arise when a higher-layer QDID (Host) asserts spec-version features that are absent in the lower-layer QDID (Controller). The SIG Consistency Check enforces inter-layer ICS alignment across the full feature set. The fix is to align all stacked QDIDs to the same specification version — use a Host Stack QDID whose version matches the Controller QDID.
final_recommendation: Always select a Host Stack QDID whose Bluetooth specification version matches the Controller QDID version. If the customer has both v5.2 and v5.4 Host Stack QDIDs available, choose the v5.2 QDID when combining with a v5.2 Controller QDID.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting a qualification design with 16 IDL errors will result in SIG rejection. The IDLs must be resolved before the registration can be approved. Delays in catching this cost significant test lab time and re-work.
